transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, yeah, thanks for having me. I, uh, I'm hoping you can help because things are getting pretty difficult at work lately. I've been a retail salesperson at this big home goods store for a few years now—it's a good job, decent pay, and mostly I'm out on the floor dealing with customers, which I don't mind at all. But recently my manager has got me pulling more shifts in the back stockroom doing inventory. It's this huge, cavernous space with these really high, dark ceilings, and, well... what brings me in is that the second I even think there might be a bat or something flapping around back there, my heart just absolutely jumps into my throat. 

I instantly start sweating buckets, like completely soaking through my work shirt—which is pretty embarrassing if I have to go back out on the sales floor—and I get this intense, overwhelming feeling that I need to get out right then. I mean, right that exact second. I'll just drop whatever boxes or clipboard I'm holding and bolt for the loading dock doors. It's like my brain just completely shorts out the moment I imagine one of those things up in the rafters, or if I see a shadow move out of the corner of my eye. I can't even stop myself from panicking, it just happens so fast...
Have you ever had these kinds of panic feelings — like your heart racing, sweating, and needing to escape — in other situations where there weren't any bats or shadows in the stockroom?

No, no, I mean... I really don't think so. It's not like I'm just an anxious guy in general, you know? Like, if I'm out on the sales floor and it's Black Friday and there's a hundred people yelling about blenders being out of stock, I'm totally fine. My heart doesn't race, I don't sweat—well, maybe a little from running around, but not that cold, panicky sweat, you know? It's really just... it's just the bats. Or the thought of the bats. 

I mean, I've tried to think back if there was ever a time I felt like that somewhere else, like maybe stuck in traffic or in a crowded elevator, because I know some people get weird about that stuff. My cousin Brenda, she can't even get in an elevator without having a whole meltdown, but for me? Nothing. I can ride elevators all day. I can sit in bumper-to-bumper traffic on the interstate for two hours and just listen to the radio, totally calm. It's literally just that specific feeling, that absolute terror, when I'm in that stockroom and I look up at those dark rafters. Or even if I'm just at home, sitting on my couch watching TV, and a commercial comes on for, like, a Halloween movie or something with a bat in it... even then, I get a little jolt, but the full-blown panic, the dropping everything and running, that's really just tied to the stockroom or places where I think they might actually be hiding. So, yeah, to answer your question, no, I don't get those feelings out of nowhere or in other situations. It's always, always connected to the bats.

latest_inference.note: The patient's panic reactions are specifically tied to the presence or thought of bats in the stockroom or similar environments, with no evidence of panic in other situations like crowds, elevators, or traffic. This rules out panic disorder, agoraphobia, social anxiety, and adjustment disorder with anxiety. The specificity of the fear to bats confirms a specific phobia (animal type).
